findings.title: Mac-sleep-as-host recorder coverage rule makes the scenario unpassable if read literally
findings.claim: The new recorder contract says complete observer coverage must span the fencing and attempted-resume interval, and any gap makes the fencing claim NOT_RUN or FAIL. During real sleep, the observer on the sleeping Mac also stops, so its record always has a gap across the very interval in which lease loss happens. Per-machine monotonic ordering is mandated, but on macOS the common monotonic sources (mach_absolute_time / process.hrtime) do not advance during sleep. The spec does not say which side's observations cover the asleep interval, or how the sleeping machine shows that its coverage resumed before any old-authority publication or command acceptance.
findings.evidence: spec L134 (monotonic ordering per machine, UTC only an annotation); L136 ('A complete observer-coverage record spans the fencing and attempted-resume interval; gaps make the fencing claim NOT_RUN or FAIL'); L143 (Mac sleep as host: 'record lease loss or service generation change while asleep, and old authority fencing on wake before it can publish or accept commands').
findings.why: Read one way, Mac sleep as host can never PASS. Read another way, an implementer quietly waives coverage. Either way the Gate F sleep evidence is not comparable between implementers.
findings.fix: State that the asleep interval is covered by the Windows peer's recorder and the service snapshots: lease expiry, generation change and rejection of old-generation traffic. The sleeping Mac's coverage obligation starts at its first wake/resume event (powerMonitor resume or an equivalent main-process lifecycle event), and that event must be recorded before any old-authority gate-open, publication or command-application event. Make it a recorded sleep-boundary event pair (suspend seen or last pre-sleep event, then resume) rather than a gap that fails the claim. Add wall-clock or continuous-clock deltas around the boundary as annotations only.

prior.note: L117 defines the logical identity field by field: commit, committed blob IDs for both lockfiles, LF-normalized contentDigest, mode, protocol/sim/checkpoint/replay, and origin. L119 makes raw sourceFiles, outputs, binaries and archives per-side, and requires CRLF/LF pairing fixtures. L121 separates deployed-Worker provenance from locally rebuilt bundle/config bytes. The docs-commit allowance at L117 matches the existing ancestor check at internet-app-smoke.ts:L88-L89 and the provenance join at internet-app-report.ts:L93-L94.

L125-L128 require a Finder-launched packaged-app session in each host direction for both D and E. The checklist covers hashes, timestamps, screenshots, room-code join, both seats acting, pause/resume and graceful exit. It is kept separate from the instrumented dev-Electron capture, and L130 says instrumentation alone never proves packaged networking.

L130 keeps the 540 s capture, the 600 s total and the existing array caps (matching internet-app-smoke.ts:L26-L30 and internet-app-report.ts:L18-L21). It assigns the ten-minute soak only to the manual packaged session (L127), and makes overflow a failed capture. Gate D at L76 is updated to match.

L134-L149 add a versioned two-machine recorder with bounds and a shared starting tuple: run ID, seat/connection generations, host generation, checkpoint sequence/capturedTick/payload SHA, and a publication. Per-scenario observations cover rehost tick at or after capturedTick under the new generation, old-authority fencing and stale rejection, and OS evidence for killed hosts. Manual and instrumented proof are labelled separately, and actualOsSuspend is declared insufficient. One new P2 about sleep-interval coverage is raised separately.

L19 and L92 no longer call the archive optional. L153 mandates a ditto ZIP keeping the parent bundle, with symlinks preserved and the whole-archive SHA as the package identity. The executable and app.asar hashes are retained separately. The extracted copy must pass an inventory comparison (paths, hashes, modes, symlink targets), a signature check and a launch.

L155 pins identity '-', disables auto-discovery, and sets notarize false and hardenedRuntime true. It names the three cs.* entitlements for the app and inherited helpers and excludes sandbox/camera/mic. L157 defines the codesign --verify --deep --strict, ad-hoc display and lipo/file ARM64 checks, and records spctl rejection separately.

L61 now says 'shared constants (including constants to be introduced below)'. L161 correctly states that SESSION_PROTOCOL_VERSION and SIM_VERSION exist and that CHECKPOINT_VERSION and SUPPORTED_REPLAY_VERSIONS must be added. It ties the schema literals and types to them, requires manifest-equality tests, and keeps historical validators (e.g. sim literal 35 at internet-app-report.ts:L12) unchanged.

L163 adds npm --prefix services/signalling ci and the build step, plus a native darwin-arm64 workerd preflight before Gate B. It records local Worker hashes apart from the deployed record, states that these are test-only prerequisites, and makes install failures explicit prerequisite failures.

L167-L169 require an owned POSIX process group and PID/PPID/PGID plus start-identity tracking with continuous sampling, so reparented helpers stay attributable. Escalation is bounded and group-scoped. Absence is verified by the deadline even when the root exits first, reused PIDs are guarded against, and inventories are retained. Success, failure, timeout and parent-exits-first cases are covered. This addresses the direct-child-only kill in lease-smoke-lifecycle.ts:L29-L31.

verified: The diff only touches L1 (BOM removed), L19, L61, L63, L76, L92, L110 and the new L113-L169 amendments. L110 states that the amendments supersede less-specific text above, which settles the remaining loose wording at L47 and L65.
Gate A (L73: 'no need to run a local Worker to play a packaged client') is consistent with L163 (local workerd is a test prerequisite only).

L117's docs-commit/ancestor allowance matches the existing tooling: internet-app-smoke.ts:L88-L89 (merge-base --is-ancestor plus exact source bytes) and internet-app-report.ts:L85-L94 (runtimeProvenance reportRevision/candidateRevision).

L130's bounds match the existing v1 limits in internet-app-smoke.ts:L26-L30 and internet-app-report.ts:L18-L21; the existing version literals (sim 35, checkpoint 2, replay 2/3/4) are at internet-app-report.ts:L12.

The instrumented session still uses dev Electron against out/ (L128), which is compatible with the electron==='37.10.3' status check the existing harness performs. The packaged session is kept strictly separate.

No amendment conflicts with the fixed decisions: no Developer account, notarize false (L155), the existing architecture is kept, and no wire-protocol fields are added (L117 'evidence-level comparisons, not new wire admission fields').
not_verified: Whether the lockfile-resolved electron-builder 26 accepts mac.identity '-' as ad-hoc signing and applies entitlementsInherit to all helper bundles. Checking this means reading node_modules, which this review is not allowed to do; the responder says it checked the entitlement template.
Whether ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc output keeps extended attributes needed by codesign after extraction. This needs native macOS execution.
Whether Electron helpers on macOS ever leave the parent's process group (affects L167's 'descendant leaves the group' path). This needs native observation.

Whether the existing `git status --porcelain` dirty flag (online-recovery-smoke.ts:L129, rtc-config-smoke.ts:L37) treats untracked non-source files as dirty in a way that conflicts with L117's 'uncommitted candidate source changes are forbidden'. This is outside the touched regions.
